_Hints for reviewers:_

- The old static `eip4844.CalcBlobFee` got changed to now require the L1 chain config and header, because the blob config now changes with Prague. However, at most places we don't have the L1 chain config available. So I added a helper `eth.CalcBlobFeeDefault` that is contend with just the header and uses the default Ethereum prod blob config and determines whether Prague is active depending on the withdrawal-requests being nil.
    - We don't need to support non-default blob schedules with the OP-Stack for now, so I deem this an acceptable workaround. Non-trivial work is needed if we need to support custom blob schedules. We can in such a case revisit this solution.
- removed some duplications of the EIP-2935 constants and just used upstream constants.
- `maxBlobsPerBlock` now depends on active fork. Adapted to either just use Cancun max in tests, or require max to be below Prague max (in batcher config checks).
    - We don't have the L1 chain config available in action testing batcher and it's not worth the effort getting there for the multi-blob tests that we run, which work just fine with 6 = cancun-max.
- replaced most uses of `core.IntrinsicGas` with `core.FloorDataGas` where calldata gas limits were estimated.
    - Just ignored if it's for a pre-Prague L1 tx, as this is just the gas _limit_ and the chain config was often not available. Not worth the effort.
- reverted #14517 to just use `core.FloorDataGas` instead

This function, as well as the associated functions added with it, allows for a configuration to be solvated with a solvent of choice, from a database of solvents stored in autode and a corresponding solvent density database in mlptrain. Alternatively, one can also specify their own solvent molecule and desired density. 

The solvation is done using a k-d tree algorithm, which is much faster than naive checking of distances in all three coordinates when adding new, and randomly rotated solvents to the box. 

Currently only implemented for cubic boxes but this is easy to change.

author: yashmayya
body:
- The query service port for a server (used for MSE queries) can change across server restarts.
- There is currently an edge case scenario with the failure detector mechanism (See https://github.com/apache/pinot/pull/15005, https://github.com/apache/pinot/pull/8491 for background) in a scenario where there are MSE queries pre server restart that have established gRPC channels to the server host / port, and there aren't any MSE queries post server restart. Here, if an SSE query failure triggers the failure detector mechanism to mark the server as unhealthy, the server won't be marked as healthy until the retry period ends or if an MSE query is sent and a new gRPC channel is established to the server's new query service port.
- This patch fixes the issue to not use stale host / port information for the failure detector's retry mechanism.

author: mpryc
body:
Implements approvals for the NaBSL objects.

Feature which allow to approve NaBSL by the cluster admin prior to the BSL creation.

Depends-on: https://github.com/openshift/oadp-operator/pull/1633

## Why the changes were made

To implement approvals for the cluster admin as described in the https://github.com/migtools/oadp-non-admin/issues/204

Fixes https://github.com/migtools/oadp-non-admin/issues/220

## How to test the changes made

### Run simulation tests

### Disable the feature
1. Deploy oadp operator with the following PR: https://github.com/openshift/oadp-operator/pull/1633
2. Set the DPA to:
```yaml
  nonAdmin:
    enable: true
    requireAdminApprovalForBSL: false
```
3. Nothing should be changed from the user perspective, on the cluster in the openshift-adp namespaces there will be `NonAdminBackupStorageLocationRequest` objects with approved flag
4. Modifying the NaBSLRequest objects and seting them to anything else then approve will make those reverted back to approve state.

### Enable the feature
1. Deploy oadp operator with the following PR: https://github.com/openshift/oadp-operator/pull/1633
2. Set the DPA to:
```yaml
  nonAdmin:
    enable: true
    requireAdminApprovalForBSL: true
```
3. Creating NaBSL should result in the condition not satisfied and requires admin to approve the NaBSLRequest object
4. Update the corresponding NaBSLRequest and set the:
```yaml
spec:
  approvalDecision: approve
```
5. NaBSL should be created
6. Patch the NaBSLRequest and set the flag to:
```yaml
spec:
  approvalDecision: reject # or pending
```
7. The NaBSL should be updated to reflect the decision, corresponding Velero BSL and Secret in the openshift-adp namespace shoud be removed.

### Update the NaBSL spec
This change disallows to update NaBSL spec as a result test can be performed to update spec that was already created. Changes to the spec will result in the BSL to being removed from the cluster and the user informed.
